section.title: Introduction
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.artifacts identifies possible decoding errors, control characters, and hidden Unicode characters. Each finding has a type and UTF-16 offsets into the original text. Detection does not change the text. Callers can inspect, mask, or repair the reported spans.

The built-in detector reports these types, each a constant on TextArtifact: replacement (U+FFFD runs), control (control characters that are not whitespace), noncharacter, unpaired-surrogate, private-use, bidi-control (explicit directional overrides and isolates), zero-width, unicode-tag (characters from the Unicode Tags block outside the flag syntax described below), and mojibake (a stretch for which the reverse single-byte mapping produces valid multibyte UTF-8).

A single zero-width character between letters is left unreported, even when combining marks intervene. This includes joining controls in words from scripts such as Malayalam and Sinhala. A single joiner next to a pictograph or emoji variation selector is also left unreported. Runs of two or more zero-width characters are reported.

The Unicode-tag exception requires U+1F3F4 BLACK FLAG, a region or subdivision code, and U+E007F CANCEL TAG. The code syntax follows UTS #51 and UTS #35: two lowercase region letters followed by one to four lowercase letters or digits, or three region digits with an optional suffix of one to four lowercase letters or digits. Longer tag runs are reported. The detector does not check whether CLDR assigns the code.

These are detection heuristics, not language or security validation. Bidi controls, private-use characters, and other reported characters can be intentional. Inspect findings before deleting or replacing text.
